articles.title: Wicked surprise: On the northeast monsoon
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. For instance, December 1, 2015, saw the city of Chennai deluged by its heaviest rainfall in 24-hours in over a century ; at least 500 lives were lost and 18 lakh people displaced in the State. That year and the present are linked by a common thread: a powerful El Niño. Associated with the heating up of the Central Pacific, the El Niño is linked to the drying up of the southwest monsoon rains but also yoked — not always — with a vigorous northeast monsoon. Other than in 2015, several El Niño years, such as 1997 and 2009, have been associated with above-normal rainfall between October and December in Tamil Nadu though El Niño years, such as 2002 and 1982, saw a poor northeast monsoon (and a predictably bad southwest monsoon). While the climate mechanisms linking a vigorous northeast monsoon and El Niño are still to be fully understood, it appears the warming patterns of the El Niño tend to deflect rain-bearing cyclonic circulations in unpredictable ways. Therefore, the Centre and the southern States ought to take enough precautions: from clearing up stormwater drains, fortifying shelters, making provisions for infrastructure damage and tightening weather warning forecasts to prepare for torrents.

articles.title: In the crossfire: on India and the Saudi-Houthi conflict
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The killing of an Indian national in a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Dammam airport is a grim reminder of the dangers the kingdom’s Indian community faces as the conflict between Riyadh and Yemen’s Shia militants escalates. Since the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis resumed in July, at least two Indians have been killed and 14 others wounded. On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that a yacht with 14 Indians was targeted by Saudi forces near Yemen’s Zuqar island in the Red Sea and that rescue operations were under way. As the Houthis, who control parts of Northern Yemen and its entire Red Sea coast, step up attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including oil facilities and airports, Indians, who are the kingdom’s largest expat community, risk getting caught in the crossfire. With flights disrupted, thousands of Indian pilgrims are stranded. India has condemned Houthi attacks, saying that it “stands in solidarity” with Saudi Arabia. With no end in sight to the fighting and a high possibility of Israel and the U.S. resuming their Iran strikes, further violence and instability in West Asia could make India’s choices increasingly difficult.

The Saudi-Houthi conflict dates back to the Houthi takeover of Sana’a, Yemen’s capital, in 2014. A year later, Saudi Arabia began bombing Yemen to drive the Houthis out. But years of Saudi bombing of one of the poorest Arab countries have proved counterproductive; the Houthis consolidated support among the tribes of northern Yemen and built a powerful territorial army and naval force. The Saudi-Houthi ceasefire of 2022 collapsed in July 2026 after Saudi Arabia recklessly bombed Sana’a airport, to prevent an Iranian plane with a Houthi delegation from landing. The Houthis subsequently began attacking Saudi Arabia’s critical infrastructure, and launched a ground offensive against the Saudi-backed forces in Yemen. The Houthi attacks pose the biggest security challenge to Mohammed bin Salman, Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince and the main architect of the war on Yemen, in decades. Massive Saudi air strikes have neither defeated the Houthis nor restored the kingdom’s deterrence. With its wealth, natural resources, infrastructure and tenuous palace politics, the kingdom remains exposed to Houthi missile and drone attacks, with few good options for a way out. India must prepare a contingency plan for worst-case scenarios. Its immediate priority should be to evacuate stranded Indian pilgrims. It should also articulate a stronger position for stability and work with Arab countries and Tehran to push for a diplomatic settlement to the Iran crisis . For peace to prevail in the Persian Gulf, the guns directed at Iran must first fall silent.

articles.title: Falling short: on Marco Rubio’s second visit to India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The United States Secretary of State’s three-day visit to India , his second in five months, came at a significant time in U.S. politics. Marco Rubio’s Mumbai trip this week was just ahead of the U.S. midterm elections , which would mark the midpoint of President Donald Trump’s second term in office — a point at which the incumbent normally begins to focus on legacy, and possible contenders for the next Presidential election (Mr. Rubio is expected to be one), and start to look for possible partners and friendships around the world. In addition, his visit also raised hopes in New Delhi of a reset in bilateral ties, battered by two years of uncertainty over the Trump administration’s actions. This would include positive moves towards concluding the Bilateral Trade Agreement , reassuring India about U.S. sanctions on the import of Russian oil, preparations for upcoming Trump meets with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Manila (ASEAN) and Miami (G-20) summits, discussing plans for the Quad Summit (on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit) that India has been trying to host, and setting a date for Mr. Trump’s India visit. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s invitation also offered Mr. Rubio an opportunity to meet their UAE counterpart, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to discuss the Gulf situation and to restore energy security and connectivity. And finally, Mr. Rubio’s visit to the Jamnagar Reliance refinery, led to speculation of some major deals on energy, possibly offering more discounts as he pitched for India to buy more American and U.S.-licensed Venezuelan oil.

Given all the high expectations, the visit was bound to come up short. The optics of his visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar, but not New Delhi, which was announced by the U.S. Ambassador to India , gave the Opposition fodder to question the real purpose of the visit. Despite Mr. Rubio’s two visits to India and more than six by Mr. Jaishankar to the U.S. since Mr. Trump took office, relations remain on edge, with issues on trade, tariffs, H-1B restrictions and anti-immigrant measures unaddressed. Also, the U.S.’s narrative on Operation Sindoor (2025), growing ties with Pakistan, and the Trump administration’s rhetoric on India’s economy, diaspora and Russian oil trade have added to India’s unhappiness. The two sides did not announce any agreements and Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Rubio did not hold a joint press address. However, as they did at the U.S. Independence Day’s 250th anniversary celebrations in Delhi in May, they attended the “Freedom 250” event in Mumbai. Mr. Rubio acknowledged that while no two countries would agree on all issues, he said the U.S.-India alignment on core issues of national interest was “extraordinary” . From this point on, Mr. Rubio must walk that talk, with a view to ensuring that India-U.S. ties are able to move on from the difficulties of the last few years.

articles.title: Canary in the coal mine: On the performance of India’s core industrial sectors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The latest data on the performance of the core industrial sectors show the economy may be facing an industrial uptick, but questions about its sustainability remain. Growth in the Index of Core Industries rose to a series-high of 7.9% in September 2026, the second consecutive month of accelerated performance. Any such improvement is to be celebrated, but a deeper look at what is driving it is also warranted. The coal sector saw growth suddenly shoot up to 10.7% in September. The unexpected and unusual nature of this rapid acceleration can be borne out by the fact that the sector contracted by 1.1% over the longer April-September 2026 period. The growth in coal in September was likely a temporary blip aided by a statistical low base and, more importantly, pressure from power plant operators over rapidly depleting coal stocks amid the heat wave. The electricity sector grew 11.4% in September, capping off a half-year dominated by double-digit growth. This surge in electricity-related demand for coal will likely wane, especially since the El Niño factor that drove the heat wave will also result in a milder winter. The other sector that results in high coal usage, the steel sector, did accelerate in September, but not by enough to sustain the coal sector’s September output. The uptick in steel did, however, result in a return to double-digit growth for the iron ore sector, which should bode well for the mining component of the larger Index of Industrial Production.

The performance of the crude oil, natural gas, and refinery products sectors also highlights the fiscal problems India faces. At a time when the crude oil and natural gas sectors have both contracted continuously since 2024, refinery output rose to 10.3% in September. This means that the refineries were increasingly processing expensive imported oil. India’s oil imports in September were up 7% by volume but jumped 47% in terms of value due to the high price of oil. This is set to worsen. The attacks on Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure have already pushed global oil prices above $112 a barrel, almost a six-month high. The reprieve from the U.S. on potential tariffs linked to imports of Russian oil provide India a reliable source, but the days of discounts are long gone. It is the time of premium pricing, and each barrel imported is eating into India’s foreign exchange reserves, which are also being used to defend the rupee. Cement and steel are the only sustainably growing core sectors, and those too are based on government infrastructure spending. At a time when industrial output is only temporarily propped up, the government’s fiscal space is fast shrinking.

articles.title: Tunnelling through: On China’s export control list, tunnel-boring machines
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs decision to place tunnel-boring machines (TBMs) on an export control list reveals a blind spot in India’s supply chain diversification. The curbs include TBMs, walking excavators, and high-altitude wet shotcrete machines. From November 18, if a shipment is intended for countries or regions deemed sensitive due to ongoing disputes with China, exporters will need an export licence from commerce authorities. For other countries/regions, exporters will need to be registered, obtain an export certificate, and submit end-use declarations stating that the equipment will not be re-routed to sensitive locations. While China has cornered around 70% of the global TBM market, prominent manufacturers in the West also maintain substantial component supply chains in the country to cut manufacturing overhead. Further, TBMs are complex to build as they have to be configured to geological characteristics at the project site and perform numerous tasks. Where a suitable TBM exists, it can be used for civilian or military purposes. India has struggled with TBM-related hold-ups with China for at least two years now, including for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail project. Germany’s Herrenknecht AG set up an assembling and refurbishing facility in Chennai in 2007-08. TBM production economics differ significantly from conventional construction equipment as new plants need a minimum number of orders and must be able to access the industrial capability required to design, manufacture and repair specialised components.

However, even though India is one of the world’s largest TBM importers, expecting every sophisticated machine to be produced domestically will send public infrastructure costs soaring. Even now, depending on China’s decision on the TBMs set for India, India may have to redirect its procurement to facilities based directly in Germany or Japan, say, and absorb the higher capital cost. The BEML experience shows that manufacturing partnerships can fail without secure licensing arrangements and access to sustained demand. India should pursue domestic manufacturing alongside international partnerships, e.g., making equipment in the country under agreement with established foreign firms, and develop shared industrial capabilities rather than singular ‘national champions’, as TBM manufacturers and their suppliers can benefit from access to common testing and precision manufacturing infrastructure. Overall, Beijing is systematically identifying sectors where it commands a significant global capacity and establishing export controls to counter western technological restrictions, such as on advanced semiconductors, so any critical infrastructure sector relying on Chinese supply lines will face a compounding geopolitical risk.

articles.title: Kuttiadi eyes river circuit to tap tourism potential
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tourism department and the Kozhikode district administration are considering a proposal to develop a river tourism circuit connecting local bodies through which the Kuttiadi river flows, with a view to promoting river and hill tourism in the Kuttiadi Assembly constituency.

A meeting chaired by Kuttiadi MLA Parakkal Abdulla was recently held to discuss the proposal. The MLA submitted a comprehensive report on the tourism potential of rivers, ponds, paddy fields and hills in the constituency to District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty, with the aim of promoting the region’s overall development.
The meeting decided to organise a joint river expedition involving the District Collector, the MLA, grama panchayat presidents and tourism officials to explore the region’s tourism potential.

A team of experts from the Tourism department is expected to visit the proposed locations soon to assess their feasibility. A team led by the District Collector will subsequently visit the shortlisted sites.
The meeting also decided to take urgent steps to improve facilities at Payamkuttimala and widen the road leading to the hill.

articles.title: Suspected kingpin of drug network held in Malappuram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A special police team arrested Ibrahim Badusha, 29, alleged kingpin of a drug trafficking network operating across Keralam and other States, from a hideout at Kolathur in Malappuram district on Monday (October 26).

A native of Kadambode, Panthalloor, Mr. Badusha is suspected of playing a key role in the network linked to the seizure of 12.8 kg of MDMA from Coimbatore. The police had arrested three men with the drugs, valued at more than ₹10 crore in the retail market, concealed in the door panels of a car, in August this year.

The seizure followed an investigation into a drug network exposed after six people were arrested with 100 gm of suspected MDMA from a private apartment in Manjeri. Interrogation of the accused led investigators to Mr. Badusha and other members of the network.
Police said the gang sourced and stored large quantities of MDMA in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru before transporting them for distribution in Keralam and Tamil Nadu.

Luxury cars fitted with concealed compartments were allegedly used to move the drugs to transit points, including Coimbatore, Palani and Kodaikanal, before smaller consignments were delivered to different locations.

Investigators identified Mr. Badusha as a key intermediary for the network in Malappuram. Police said that more than 200 kg of MDMA had been smuggled into Keralam under his leadership over the past six months.

Another alleged kingpin, Akhil Joy, a native of Wayanad and a close associate of Mr. Badusha, was arrested from Bihar about a month ago. Mr. Badusha is also an accused in cases involving murder, drug trafficking and theft in Wayanad and Malappuram districts, police said.

After the investigation began, Mr. Badusha allegedly went into hiding in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Odisha and Chennai. Bengaluru Police were also looking for him after he reportedly abandoned a car in Electronic City following a collision involving around 10 vehicles.

The special investigation team (SIT), including officers from the Malappuram and Perinthalmanna police sub-divisions, the Narcotics Cell and the District Anti-Narcotic Special Action Force (DANSAF), carried out the arrest.
Police said the investigation was continuing to trace the source of the drugs and identify other members of the network.

articles.title: Kannur panchayat contracts: KSU vice-president challenges allegations, threatens legal action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kerala Students Union (KSU) State vice-president P. Muhammed Shammas has challenged Carton India Alliance Private Limited managing director Mohammed Asif to produce evidence for the allegations against him and threatened legal action, escalating the controversy over alleged irregularities in contracts awarded by the Kannur district panchayat.

The confrontation comes amid a fresh vigilance investigation into alleged irregularities in public works contracts worth more than ₹12 crore awarded to the company. The Keralam government sanctioned the investigation on October 23 against former district panchayat president P.P. Divya, her husband V.P. Ajith and former district panchayat secretary Abdul Latheef, following a complaint by Mr. Shammas. The probe was authorised under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Addressing the media in Kannur, Mr. Shammas said he had been raising allegations of corruption and benami transactions for nearly two years and had submitted complaints and supporting documents to the authorities.
Responding to allegations that he had sought money through an intermediary, he said the claims had changed from an initial allegation of a demand for money to one involving ₹5 lakh.

“Let them not think that they can divert the issue by raising such cheap allegations. I have placed the matters before the public and the authorities with documents and evidence. I challenge Mohammed Asif to produce the evidence on which his allegations against me are based,” he said.
Mr. Shammas said he would initiate legal action against Mr. Asif over what he described as a malicious campaign.

Mr. Shammas questioned the relationship between Ms. Divya and Carton India Alliance, as well as Mr. Asif’s association with the company. He referred to audio recordings and WhatsApp screenshots that he claimed raised questions about their alleged links.

He cited a voice message in which Mr. Asif allegedly asked someone to meet Binoy Kurian, then district panchayat vice-president, reportedly at Ms. Divya’s direction. Mr. Shammas said the recordings and related material had been brought to the attention of the authorities, including the Vigilance department.

Responding to the allegations, Mr. Kurian denied that contracts had been awarded without following tender procedures. He said the district panchayat had invited tenders from project management consultants in 2022-23, with three companies participating and SILK being selected for quoting the lowest percentage charge.
SILK subsequently prepared estimates and invited tenders to select executing agencies, including Carton India Alliance, he said.

“The district panchayat has no role in selecting Carton India. That responsibility rests with SILK,” Mr. Kurian said, adding that the prescribed procedures had been followed and the relevant files were available for public scrutiny at the district panchayat office.

articles.title: Madras High Court denies anticipatory bail to Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in ₹100-crore private schools fraud case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Madras High Court on Monday (October 26, 2026) denied anticipatory bail to former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi of the DMK in a corruption case after observing that the final destination of over ₹400 crore, allegedly collected towards a ‘party fund’ from over 177 private school managements in the State, could be found out only if he is subjected to custodial interrogation.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan said he was of the view that grant of advance bail to the former Minister would paralyse the investigation being conducted by the Central Crime Branch for offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

“While protection of individual liberty is a duty of the court, it should be weighed against the society’s need for a corruption-free governmental administration,” he said. Rejecting the petitioner’s argument that all evidence in the case was documentary in nature, and hence, his arrest was not absolutely necessary in such a case, the judge said: “Money trails would still require custodial interrogation in order to establish the intent and identify who had been holding the strings and the final destination of the amount alleged to be involved.”

Further, the judge recorded the submission of State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan that the second accused Muthukumar, who was a classmate of the former Minister and also the treasurer of a private schools association through which the ‘party fund’ was collected, was still absconding and his whereabouts could be found out only by interrogating the present petitioner. “The petitioner is a politician, holding a high position. If anticipatory bail is granted before the second accused is apprehended, then it would become a tool for the second accused to avoid the process of the investigation. As the investigation is still at its nascent stage and as new facts are being unearthed, this court is of the view that grant of anticipatory bail would not be fit and proper,” Justice Lakshminarayanan said.

He went on to state that corruption was a grave economic offence. “It not only affects the public exchequer but is also a crime against humanity and directly affects the human rights. In cases such as these, the court has to keep in mind the position that had been occupied by the petitioner and thereby his ability to tamper with the State machineries or influence witnesses.”

He also said courts would generally be slow in granting anticipatory bail in corruption cases, especially when a strong apprehension arose that the petitioner could use the liberty to influence witnesses, hamper investigation, or destroy physical evidence. “In the present case, prima facie, the records reveal that the absconding accused — A2 has been shielded by the petitioner,” he wrote.

The judge said Justices J.B. Pardiwala and R. Mahadevan of the Supreme Court had in 2025 held that in corruption cases, anticipatory bail could not be sought as a matter of right, and it could be granted only in cases involving political vendetta, false implications, or manifest frivolity. “None of the exceptions pointed out by Pardiwala J. applies to the facts of the present case,” he concluded.

According to the CCB, the first and second accused were the founder president and treasurer respectively of an unregistered body titled ‘Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association’. They were instrumental in collecting crores of rupees from various private school managements for purposes such as gaining permanent recognition, upgradation , DTCP/CMDA approvals, building related permissions and other government approvals.

Investigation reveals collection of ‘party fund’ during Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi’s tenure as School Education Minister, CCB tells Madras High Court

The investigating agency claimed the unregistered association was formed in 2024 on the basis of the former Minister’s communication through his personal assistant Valadi Karthick. Mr. Poyyamozhi had participated in the event held for inaugurating the association at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024. Claiming that it had secured the video footage of the event, the CCB said, the then Minister had “projected” Mr. Arasakumar and Mr. Muthukumar before a large gathering of school correspondents.

Thereafter, all the needs of individual school managements were routed through the first two accused for being placed before the higher government level. So far, “more than 177 victim school managements have come forward and a prima facie amount of ₹17,26,73,650 has been traced. The complete financial trail and ultimate beneficiaries is still under investigation,” the CCB told the court.

articles.title: Virtual autopsy at Kozhikode Medical College Hospital: launch likely to take time
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The proposed launch of virtual autopsy (virtopsy), an advanced forensic technique, at the Government Medical College Hospital (MCH), Kozhikode, is likely to take some more time as the work in this regard is still in progress.

According to official sources, one of the members from the Department of Forensic Medicine at the hospital recently underwent a month-long training in the subject at the North-Eastern Hill Indira Gandhi Regional Institute of Health and Medical Sciences, Shillong, Meghalaya, which is a pioneer in virtual autopsy in the country.

The department has also submitted a detailed list of the facilities to be introduced at the hospital, including the staff to be appointed and the equipment to be installed, to the government. The sources said that discussions are also ongoing with experts at the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi.

The main objectives of an autopsy are determining the cause and manner of death, establishing identity, and collecting evidence for litigation and investigation. Virtual autopsy reports are almost identical to traditional autopsy reports, the difference is only in the use of advanced imaging instead of invasive dissection. Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) technologies are used for this non-invasive procedure, where three-dimensional data of the entire body, or relevant parts, are created to examine the details. However, forensic experts point out that in suspicious or unnatural deaths, a medico-legal autopsy is always mandatory.

According to Health department sources, none of the government hospitals in Keralam follows such a system at present. A.K. Unmesh, Professor, Forensic Medicine, had given a detailed project report (DPR) to the government in December 2025 to set up a virtual autopsy centre at the Government Medical College, Kottayam, where he was working then as the Head of the Department. The DPR had said that setting up such a facility would improve medico-legal services, enhance judicial transparency, reduce the stress of families by offering minimally invasive options, and provide permanent digital evidence for appeals and reviews. The plan was to enhance collaboration between departments such as Radiology and Forensic Medicine, and the judiciary and law enforcement. It was also pointed out that a digital repository of forensic imaging could be created for evidence and academic research. The total projected capital cost was ₹15.5 crore, and the recurring annual cost was estimated to be ₹2.5 crore.
After the United Democratic Front (UDF) came to power in May this year, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has repeatedly declared that the virtual autopsy system would be first launched in Kozhikode.

articles.title: BPCL shifts crude sourcing towards Middle East as Russian oil loses price edge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) tapped more into Middle Eastern crude as Russian oil lost its price advantage and also due to rising freight costs, with the shift becoming more pronounced in November, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, Director (Finance), told analysts during a post-results call on Monday.

“Our spot crude share remained at around 67% in the second quarter, while Russian grade accounted for approximately 37% of our total crude procurement, both broadly in line with the previous quarter,” Mr. Gupta said, adding that the company increased purchases from the Middle East as supplies from the region improved.

Russia accounted for 37% of BPCL’s crude basket in the September quarter, followed by Saudi Arabia at 19%, Abu Dhabi at 17%, the U.S. at 9% and Oman at 6%. The remaining supplies came from countries contributing 1-4% each.
As of September-end, BPCL held about 22 days of crude inventory, with sourcing requirements tied up through December.
Mr. Gupta said the share of Russian crude in October was expected to remain “more or less the same”, although procurement volumes would be lower for November.

“October, our requirement from Russia slightly came down but in the month of November, the cargoes from Russia significantly reduced due to [reduced] commercial viability [compared to that from Middle East], mainly the increase in the freight,” he said, adding that the company did not receive attractive offers for Russian crude in November.

Russian crude was available at a premium of $12-$13 per barrel over benchmark prices in October. The premium has narrowed to $1-$2 per barrel for December cargoes, Mr. Gupta said, although freight costs remain high.
“Maybe today, Russian cargo is preferable than a Middle Eastern cargo for December month because November [procurement] we have already concluded,” he said.

BPCL also diversified its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sourcing during the quarter. Supplies from the Arab Gulf improved, while the US accounted for about 48% of LPG imports in the September quarter.
Softening Saudi Contract Prices (Saudi CP), the benchmark for LPG pricing, helped reduce under-recoveries to an average ₹290 per cylinder in the September quarter from ₹507 in the June quarter.

Under-recoveries are expected to be ₹245 per cylinder in October and are expected to rise to ₹328 in November, Mr. Gupta said. BPCL currently holds 32 days of LPG inventory, including supplies in transit.
The company has also diversified liquefied natural gas (LNG) procurement by increasing spot purchases from the US, Oman and West Africa.

articles.title: Anthropic files for IPO as revenue jumps 14-fold to $16.3 billion in H1
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, has filed to go public in the United States, disclosing rapid revenue growth, expanding enterprise spending and the high cost of developing and running advanced AI models.

The company filed a registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 26. It intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT”. The number of shares to be offered and the price range have not yet been determined.
The public filing follows Anthropic’s confidential submission of a draft registration statement to the SEC on June 1, 2026. The proposed IPO remains subject to regulatory review.

One of the key disclosures is that revenue from a group of existing customers was about nine times higher in the three months ended September 30, 2026, than in the same period a year earlier. The calculation includes customers who generated at least $1 in revenue in the earlier period but excludes subscribers to Anthropic’s Claude Pro and Max plans.

The company reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September 30, up from more than 950 a year earlier. More than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million, while approximately 250 generated at least $10 million.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.16 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. Its net loss widened to $80.7 billion from $13 billion, largely because of accounting expenses arising from changes in the estimated value of certain financing instruments as the company’s valuation rose.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $693 million in the first half of 2026, compared with $2.14 billion a year earlier. However, using its own adjusted measure, which excludes certain expenses, the company reported operating income of $1.6 billion, with a margin of about 10%.

It reported $8.95 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses in the first half of 2026, reflecting the costs of developing and running advanced AI models. As of June 30, the company held $131.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, according to the filing.
ALSO WATCH Anthropic loses over $80 billion in first half of 2026

The prospectus flags risks including dependence on computing infrastructure providers, competition and the cost of developing increasingly capable AI models. Major cloud providers supply Anthropic with computing capacity and help distribute its products, while also developing competing AI services.

The filing also outlines a governance structure intended to protect Anthropic’s long-term public-benefit mission. An entity formed by its seven co-founders will hold a special share carrying 50.1% of general voting power, while the company’s Long-Term Benefit Trust will have the right to appoint a majority of the board. This would limit the ability of ordinary shareholders to influence corporate governance, even after the company lists publicly.
Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be offered or the proposed price range. The timing and terms of the IPO will depend on the regulatory process and market conditions.

articles.title: Russia says open to mini Ukraine ceasefires, but no letup in war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Russia said Monday (October 26, 2026) that it would not slow down its offensive on Ukraine despite upcoming U.S.-brokered talks on ending the conflict but that it could agree local "humanitarian" ceasefires.
The Kremlin said that it was open to short-term "humanitarian" ceasefires along the front line, ahead of a truce in the ravaged Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

A ceasefire is to start in the southern Ukrainian city early Tuesday (October 27), brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump after months of reports that residents faced dire food, water and medicine shortages.
Asked whether Russia would consider more local truces, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters: "For humanitarian purposes, absolutely."
But Moscow vowed not to let up in the overall pace of the war, even as the sides prepare to restart stalled talks under U.S. mediation next month.
"The decision to resume trilateral talks does not imply any restrictions on combat operations," Mr. Peskov said.
"Our armed forces continue to carry out massive strikes on Ukraine's military-industrial complex," he added.

Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, hitting energy sites around major cities in what Kyiv says is a bid to plunge the country into cold and darkness throughout the winter.
Strikes last year left millions without heating or electricity with temperatures as low as -20C.
The two sides are to meet next month with U.S. envoys to discuss ways to end Europe's worst conflict since World War II.
Several previous rounds have failed to move the sides closer to a deal. Russia demands more territory in eastern Ukraine and sweeping military and political restrictions on Kyiv.
Ukraine and its allies say the demands are tantamount to a capitulation that would leave the country exposed to a future Russian attack.

articles.title: Mass outages in Sudan after RSF drones hit five power stations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Sudan's Paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched a coordinated drone attack Monday (October 26, 2026) against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country's east, a government official told AFP .

The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref, and one in White Nile state, "resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states", the official said on condition of anonymity.
All three states are controlled by the Sudanese army, which has since April 2023 been at war with its former ally, the RSF.
The United Nations has repeatedly warned that regular attacks on power stations threaten health and services for millions of people, already facing the world's largest hunger crisis.
An AFP correspondent in Al-Jazira state reported the electricity had been out since 2 a.m. (0000 GMT).
Babiker Youssef, a resident of Al-Fao in Gedaref, said the power there had also been out since the same time.
"My son is diabetic; his insulin has to be stored in the fridge," he told AFP over the phone, scared he would not be able to replace the medication if it spoils.
"We have no idea when the power will come back," he added.

Electricity has been cut for days at a time after past Paramilitary drone strikes on power stations and hydroelectric dams, compounding the suffering of nearly 20 million people facing extreme hunger.
Sudan's war is currently being fought primarily via drones, with both sides launching sophisticated attacks from across the country, killing dozens of civilians at a time.
In the first three weeks of October alone, drone strikes killed over 300 people and injured hundreds more, according to a UN tally.
Africa's third-largest country, home to an estimated 50 million people, has been ravaged by the war, which aid workers estimate has killed more than 200,000 people.

articles.title: Plant-based meat yields higher share of absorbable protein than traditional meat: study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: While plant-derived kababs may still struggle to replicate the taste and texture of meat from a tandoori joint, they may contain relatively more protein in a form that the body can absorb, according to a study presented on Monday (October 26, 2026).

In a collaboration between the CSIR–Institute of Himalayan Bioresource Technology (CSIR-IHBT), Palampur, and the Good Food Institute (GFI) India, a non-profit that promotes alternative proteins such as plant-based, fermentation-derived and cultivated meat, scientists investigated whether protein bioavailability (meaning protein in a form that’s nutritively useful to the body) of traditional meat was the same as that of plant-based meat.

Tests on five cooked plant-based products — two burger patties, a nugget and two seekh kebabs — showed higher bioavailability percentages than their chicken counterparts, according to the findings presented at a press conference on Monday (October 26). The plant-based kebabs scored 80.8% and 86.1% against 38.8% for chicken. The nugget scored 61.2% against 43.4%, and the patties recorded about 57% and 58% against 21.2%.

The findings do not mean plant-based meat is healthier, but only that they are nutritively comparable, as ‘healthier’ is a subjective term, Dr. Padma Ishwarya, senior scientist at GFI India, told The Hindu . “It’s too much of a vague term. It’s too broad a term…for health, we need to do further studies.”

The chicken products held more crude protein and released more amino acids, the building blocks of protein, during digestion, and Dr. Ishwarya said more products and samples would be tested in the next phase.

The work has not yet been published as a journal paper. “It is a report that is hosted on our website, but it is very much peer-reviewed,” Dr. Ishwarya said in a conversation with The Hindu . Two experts reviewed it, she said, and it was an overview and that detailed manuscripts would follow.

The team used an in vitro method that simulated digestion in a laboratory. Samples went through a two-minute salivary phase, then a stomach phase with digestive enzymes at pH 2 to 3, and then an intestinal phase. The method follows INFOGEST, an internationally harmonised protocol, Dr. Ishwarya said.

The team added an ultrafiltration membrane chosen to mimic the pore size of the human intestine. Whatever passed through the membrane was deemed bioavailable, and only free amino acids were measured. Each sample was adjusted to start with 40 milligrammes of protein.

Animal studies remain the gold standard, she said, but are tedious and require ethical clearances. The simulated method is faster and more reproducible. The team plans to conduct tests across laboratories next year so that NABL-accredited labs can use the method.

Plant-based meat, Dr. Ishwarya said, is made “specifically for biomimicking animal-derived meat”, unlike crisps or cereals, which are plant-based foods. It is made from soya, pea or wheat gluten, mostly soya, and shaped by extrusion, a process in which material is pushed through a die under heat and pressure. She said it contains no synthetic chemicals beyond ingredients such as spices and texturisers.

The study examined only protein. An earlier analysis in 2024 of about 120 products in the Indian market, she said, found that saturated fat and sodium levels were comparable to those in animal-derived products, leaving room for reduction. Plant-based products also supplied dietary fibre, which animal-derived products do not.

articles.title: Indian publishers contest Modi government’s privacy law
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A group of 21 news publishers has challenged the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 , India’s privacy law, in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let the government identify journalists’ sources, documents show.

Prime ​Minister Narendra Modi’s government announced the implementation of the law in 2025 to protect the digital personal data of ⁠users, raising compliance requirements for platforms like Meta and Google. The publishers have said that since media outlets were not exempt, the law was an invasion of press freedom.

Media companies received assurances in an August meeting with the government that the law would protect press freedom, but not having ‌a written carve-out for journalists like in the European Union, Singapore and Britain was alarming, the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) said in a confidential filing at the Supreme Court, reviewed by Reuters .

The October 6, 2026 lawsuit, being ‌reported for the first time and due to be heard on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), is the most high-profile challenge to the government’s privacy ‌law. ⁠Until now, only free speech activists and a group of smaller news outlets had challenged it.

It also ⁠marks an unusual challenge to the government from businesses headed by Mr. Ambani and Mr. Adani, who Opposition parties allege are close to Mr. Modi and get favourable treatment — charges the businesses and the government vehemently deny.
DNPA and the media groups did not respond to requests for comment from Reuters , and neither did the IT Ministry.

The publishers are demanding that most of the ‌law’s contentious provisions, which kick in from May 2027, be quashed. They are arguing that the law could force a journalist to get prior consent from a person they want to investigate and force publishers to erase stories. They also say powers granted by the law to demand information could expose reporters’ sources.

The law would “render investigative journalism a benign and neutered recorder ‌of events,” the 698-page filing said. The provisions “constitute pre-censorship which is anathema to any democracy worth its name”.

The lawsuit ​comes amid accusations of declining press freedom in India since Mr. Modi took office in 2014. Critics say many mainstream media outlets have not done enough to scrutinise the Modi government.
India’s ranking in Reporters Without Borders’ World ⁠Press Freedom Index fell to 157 th out of 180 countries this year, from 140 th in 2014 — but the government rejects the rankings.

Modi government says it respects press freedom and says India, which has a “vibrant press and media ecosystem” of hundreds of newspapers and TV ‌channels, does not need validation from foreign bodies.

DNPA’s members include Mr. Ambani’s Network18 , which has seven digital news platforms, Mr. Adani’s NDTV and other marquee media groups, including The Hindu, the Indian Express and Times Internet , which is part of the Times of India group, publisher of India’s largest-selling English-language daily.

articles.title: The Hindu Group, Cancer Institute launch book on comprehensive cancer care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Hindu Group, in association with the Cancer Institute (WIA), Adyar, launched Cancer 360: Overview of Detection, Treatment, Palliation , a book examining cancer care from prevention and early detection to treatment, rehabilitation and palliative care. The book was launched at The Hindu office in Chennai.

N. Ram, director of The Hindu Group, launched the book alongside Suresh Nambath, editor of The Hindu . Mr. Ram handed over the first copy to E. Hemanth Raj, executive vice-chairman of Cancer Institute.

Speaking at the launch, Mr. Ram emphasised the importance of making advanced cancer care accessible and affordable. He highlighted the institute’s work in providing treatment to those who need it most and stressed the need to ensure that advances in cancer care reach patients facing barriers to treatment.

Dr. Hemanth Raj spoke about the need to translate advances in cancer research, much of which takes place in the West, into practical interventions in local settings. He also highlighted the institute’s charitable programmes, supported by donations, to help patients access treatment and facilities, and its plans to expand cancer care to reach more patients.
Arvind Krishnamurthy, professor of surgical oncology at Cancer Institute, stressed the need for continued research to improve cancer care and develop better treatments.

The book also addresses care beyond treatment. Mahalakshmi Rangabashyam Shetty, ENT surgeon and lecturer in the Department of Surgical Oncology at the institute, spoke about individualised treatment plans developed through multidisciplinary consultations. She also highlighted the need to tailor exercise and nutrition regimens to individual patients, alongside supportive services such as hospice care.

Surendran Veeraiah, professor and head of the Department of Regional Cancer Centre (RCTC), Cancer Institute, emphasised the importance of psychological support and allied services. He said the book could help make technical information on comprehensive cancer care accessible to more people.

The book features contributions from experts across oncology and allied disciplines. Its chapters cover multidisciplinary tumour boards, psychological care, onco-physiotherapy, palliative care, cancer research, speech and swallowing rehabilitation, early detection, precision treatment, pathology, nutrition and healthcare quality.
The book is available free of cost to The Hindu subscribers at https://www.thehindu.com/premium/ebook/

articles.title: Over 100 mills commence sugar production
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: As many as 107 sugar mills have commenced sugarcane crushing for the marketing season that started on October 1, 2026, according to the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association.
Sugar mills in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh have commenced crushing operations.

The previous sugar season that ended on September 30 closed with approximately 36 lakh tonnes of carryover stocks, providing a base for meeting domestic consumption requirements. As of 25 October 2026, sugar production during the current 2026–27 season had reached approximately four lakh tonnes, compared with just about 0.6 lakh tonnes on the corresponding date last year.

The Government has extended the duty-free raw sugar import window and introduced stockholding limits. These measures, together with available carryover stocks and the commencement of fresh production, contribute to ensuring adequate sugar availability for domestic consumption during the festive period, it said.

articles.title: Keralam plans Bill to regulate high treatment costs in private hospitals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Keralam government will introduce a Bill in the next Assembly session to regulate high medical treatment costs in private hospitals, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan told the Assembly on Monday (October 26, 2026).

He was responding to a question from Communist Party of India (Marxist) MLA K.N. Balagopal on the steps being taken by the government to regulate the trend of some major hospitals, in which global private equity firms now have big stakes, inflating treatment costs.

The Minister said the government agreed in principle to the need to regulate private hospitals, many of which were now under the management of foreign companies. He said that while the costs for treatment as well as room rents have increased drastically, insurance companies are at times refusing claims, causing difficulties to the common people.

Responding to another question, Mr. Muraleedharan said the government was preparing a project to transform Keralam into a health destination which will be sought after by foreigners as well as those from other States. The Principal Secretary (Health department), Director of the Health Department and the Director of Medical Education will coordinate these activities.

A major campaign for early detection and control of lifestyle diseases is also underway. As part of this, heath workers will visit houses and identify those needing attention through a survey and preliminary screening. The pilot project will be implemented in the Vattiyurkavu, Idukki and Nilambur Assembly constituencies first and later expanded across the State, said Mr. Muraleedharan.

articles.title: Dubious retreat: on the National Medical Commission and its MSMER
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has denotified and withdrawn its 2023 Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations (MSMER), diminishing the framework of penalties vis-à-vis educational standards and infrastructure at medical colleges. The move is noteworthy as the MSMER provided for fines of up to ₹5 lakh on faculty members and administrators for submitting false information. Fortunately, the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) retains the power to fine errant institutions up to ₹1 crore under the 2023 Establishment of Medical Institutions, Assessment and Rating Regulations. MSMER was lauded for its intention to crack down on the deep-seated corruption and malpractice in medical colleges, particularly over ‘ghost faculty’ and ‘ghost patients’. The NMC’s justification is that MSMER also introduced a parallel mechanism allowing undergraduate and postgraduate boards to evaluate institutions, stepping on the MARB’s toes. However, why the NMC scrapped MSMER wholesale is unclear. The 2023 Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations remain in force and include a provision to fine individual faculty members at postgraduate medical colleges. Non-compliance among medical colleges is not uncommon and seldom nipped in the bud, even as the number of medical seats swells while the transparency of the medical education system has not improved.

Notwithstanding the provision to fine individuals at postgraduate centres, the MARB and the NMC can only penalise institutions, which is harder and risks creating a perverse incentive to accommodate rather than punish, and could mitigate the fear that keeps administrators honest. MSMER also specified timelines to appeal penalties. Although the MARB regulations retain the appeal processes, their 15-day deadline could conflict with the 60-day period under the NMC Act, potentially creating legal disputes that delay penal action. There is also a telling incident. As part of a proceeding under the RTI Act, the Central Information Commission revealed last year that the NMC had stated in 2024 that MARB had neither formally assessed nor rated medical colleges and that its standard forms need not be made public. In a revised reply in October 2025, it said the responding NMC officer’s records did not include any of the corresponding reports. However, the 2023 MARB regulations require the Board to publish its latest annual assessment results. If the NMC withdrew MSMER because the powers thereunder also exist elsewhere, the public deserves to know whether the powers are also being exercised and whether the outcomes are as publicly accessible as intended. Unless the NMC has satisfactory answers for all these lacunae, the withdrawal will appear less like simplification and more like regulatory relaxation.

articles.title: A final surge: on Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s triumph in Brazil
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: At one point, it seemed almost impossible for Brazil’s 80-year-old President, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, to turn the tide after finishing second to Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of elections on October 4. In Brazil’s history, no candidate who has finished second in the first round has gone on to win the presidential run-off. Most of the candidates who dropped out after the first round were from the right. Flávio’s Liberal Party cemented its position in both houses of Congress, while right-wing candidates won several provincial elections. But Lula, a former trade unionist and organiser, who lost a finger in an accident as a teenager, was not ready to give up. Lula and his Workers’ Party identified campaign weaknesses, shifted their attention to economic issues, promised growth and welfare, and persuaded more voters to turn out for Sunday’s run-off. Lula won 51.7% of the vote against Flávio’s 48.2%, a greater lead than his victory against Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, four years ago. Over the weeks, Lula turned the right-wing’s gains in the first round against it, highlighting the threats that a Bolsonaro victory could pose to democracy and civil rights. Flávio’s campaign pledge to free his father — he is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting to overturn Lula’s 2022 victory, and impeach Supreme Court judges — only heightened the concerns of voters outside the right wing, who rallied behind a familiar face.

Lula unleashed a social media campaign to mobilise younger voters. A WhatsApp channel called ‘Lula’s Army’ with 11 million followers spread his message of continuity. He also announced plans to expand a cash payout scheme for the poor, a new debt relief package and entrepreneur-friendly measures. In the northeast, the Workers’ Party’s stronghold, he gained nearly three million votes and made considerable gains in the working-class neighbourhoods of big cities, including São Paulo. A relatively stable economic record, marked by growth and falling unemployment over the past three and a half years, also lent credibility to Lula’s appeal. His victory bucks the recent trend in South America, where Washington-aligned right-wing and conservative forces have gained ground. While Lula offers predictable stability and social and economic inclusiveness, he could also be, as the President of South America’s largest economy, a voice of resistance to Donald Trump’s imperial ambitions. At the same time, Lula will have to work with a right-wing-controlled Congress to advance his agenda. He should seek to build legislative consensus while focusing on addressing the economic challenges of Brazil, which remains one of the most unequal major world economies.

fullParagraphs: The BJP has announced a nationwide protest on Monday (October 26, 2026) against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's "indecent and offensive" remarks targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Criticising the “ Modi ka baap bhi jayega [even Modi’s father will go]” comment, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Mr. Kharge has “torn apart all norms of decorum”.

"In protest against the insulting, indecent, and offensive remarks made by the Congress national president in Patna regarding Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late father, the BJP will stage strong demonstrations tomorrow (Monday) across all state headquarters in the country," the BJP said in a statement.
The Bihar BJP also will hold protest march and effigy burning against Mr. Kharge’s statement. The march will beging at party headquerters in Patna.

Ms. Swaroopa Rani is the Jana Sena Party (JSP) aspirant for the East Godavari Zilla Parishad chairperson’s post.
The ZPTC elections are being held using electoral rolls which the cut-off date is January 1, 2026.
Ms. Swaroopa Rani had exercised her franchise in the Rajamahendravaram rural constituency in during the 2024 general elections.

However, the transfer process of her vote had not been completed in both the mandals by October 24, making it ineligible to accept her nomination papers for the ZPTC election.”

Ms. Swaroopa Rani has applied for the transfer of her vote either to Kovvur or Sithanagaram mandals hoping to contest from whichever mandal the transfer process is done before the deadline for the scrutiny of the ZPTC nominations.

articles.title: Many places in T.N., Puducherry likely to receive moderate rain on October 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Pudukottai, Sivaganga, and Ramanathapuram districts on Monday.

Heavy rain is likely to occur over isolated places in Kanniyakumari, Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Tenkasi, Virudhunagar, Madurai, Theni, Dindigul, Karur, Tiruchi, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, and Nagapattinam districts.

The remaining parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal are likely to witness moderate rain with thunderstorms and lightning at many places. Several areas are likely to witness gusty winds during the thunderstorms, at speeds reaching 40 kmph to 50 kmph.

On Tuesday, isolated places in Ramanathapuram district are likely to get heavy rain. A few places over the rest of south Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts are likely to get moderate rainfall with thunderstorms and lightning. The other areas of the State, Puducherry, and Karaikal are likely to get light rain in a few places.

The deep depression over east-central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal moved westwards and lay centred about 450 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 820 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 910 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 1,010 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), and 1,080 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh), at 5.30 p.m.

It is likely to move westwards and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east-central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by early Monday morning. It is then likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday morning.

Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach Westcentral Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 morning. It is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm, with a maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph, gusting to 140 kmph, by the forenoon of October 28.

articles.title: BJP slams Kharge over ‘indecent’ remarks on PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s remarks at a Patna event on Sunday (October 25, 2026), in which he dragged Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father, triggered a sharp reaction from senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders, who accused the principal Opposition, under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, of increasingly resorting to personal attacks against Mr. Modi and his family.
Criticising the “ Modi ka baap bhi jayega [even Modi’s father will go]” comment, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Mr. Kharge has “torn apart all norms of decorum”.

“This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family,” he said, accusing the party of having hurled insults at the Prime Minister’s mother, calling him a “merchant of death”, and mocking his poverty by addressing him as a “chaiwala” in the past.

“Under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day,” he said, alleging that repeated electoral defeats over the past 12 years had bred “desperation and frustration” within the party.

कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खरगे ने आज पटना में मोदी जी के पिताजी के बारे में अभद्र टिप्पणी कर सारी मर्यादाएँ तार-तार कर दी हैं। यह पहली बार नहीं है, जब कांग्रेस पार्टी ने मोदी जी या उनके परिवार को अपशब्द कहे हों। कभी उनकी पूजनीय माताजी के विषय में अपशब्द कहे, कभी उन्हें 'मौत का सौदागर' कहा, तो कभी 'चायवाला' कहकर उनकी गरीबी का उपहास उड़ाया। राहुल गांधी के नेतृत्व में कांग्रेस पार्टी हर रोज अभद्रता की सीमाएँ पार करती जा रही है। बीते 12 वर्षों में लगातार मिल रही चुनावी हार से कांग्रेस पार्टी में हताशा व निराशा इतनी बढ़ चुकी है कि अब उसके पास न कोई नीति बची है, न कोई मुद्दा, बस गाली-गलौज की राजनीति बची है। जनता के बीच जनाधार खो चुकी कांग्रेस, अब अपने कार्यकर्ताओं में भी आधार खोती जा रही है। जब-जब इन्होंने मोदी जी या उनके परिवार पर घृणित टिप्पणियाँ की हैं, तब-तब जनता ने कांग्रेस को करारा जवाब दिया है।

“Only the politics of slander remains. Having lost its public base among the people, Congress is now steadily losing its base even among its own workers. Whenever they have made hateful comments against Modi ji or his family, the public has given Congress a resounding response every time,” said Mr. Shah on X .

Terming Mr. Kharge’s language “indecent and unparliamentary”, BJP chief Nitin Nabin said: “There is a certain dignity to political opposition as well, but dragging the departed family members into speeches from public platforms has now become the real ‘culture’ of Rahul Gandhi and the whole Opposition. This is not Kharge ji’s personal statement, but a reflection of the entire Congress party’s lack of decorum in its thinking.”

“Frustrated by repeated electoral defeats, the Congress party is venting its political spite against Prime Minister Modi ji and his family through baseless and irresponsible comments. The Opposition’s panic — stemming from Modi ji ’s rising popularity at home and abroad, and the public’s unwavering trust in him — is now plainly evident in its language and conduct,” said Union Minister J.P. Nadda.

He said that in a democracy, opponents must not “cross the bounds of propriety”, and the people will respond to such politics. “The Congress must realise that the trust of the people cannot be won through a politics of hatred and humiliation. The people of the country will surely deliver their response to such petty politics through democratic means,” he said.

आज पटना में कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे द्वारा देश के माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के प्रति जिस प्रकार की अमर्यादित और असंसदीय भाषा का प्रयोग किया गया है, वह कांग्रेस के वैचारिक दिवालियापन को दर्शाता है। राजनीतिक विरोध की भी एक गरिमा होती है, लेकिन सार्वजनिक मंच से स्वर्गीय परिजनों को भाषणों में घसीटना ही अब राहुल गांधी और समूचे विपक्ष का असली 'संस्कार' बन चुका है। यह खड़गे जी का व्यक्तिगत बयान नहीं, बल्कि पूरी कांग्रेस की शिष्टाचार-विहीन सोच का प्रकटीकरण है। जब विपक्ष के पास देश के विकास, नीति और जनकल्याणकारी योजनाओं पर बहस करने के लिए कोई ठोस मुद्दा नहीं बचता, तो वे इसी प्रकार की हताशा और व्यक्तिगत आक्षेपों का सहारा लेते हैं। देश की जनता इस अमर्यादित राजनीति को भली-भांति देख रही है और समय आने पर इसका करारा जवाब देगी।

articles.title: Is Yashwant Varma still a judge?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Parliament is set to take up in the coming Monsoon Session the report of the Committee appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 to investigate charges of misbehaviour against former Judge of the Allahabad and Delhi High Courts, Yashwant Varma, who has since resigned. The allegations against him arise from the discovery in March 2025 of partially burnt currency notes in an outhouse at his official residence. Mystery surrounds his current status and the future course of the pending proceedings in Parliament.

On one hand, three months after his resignation, Mr. Varma continues to be listed by the Allahabad High Court and by the Department of Justice of the Union government as a sitting judge. This has given rise to misgivings about whether his resignation has taken effect or remains subject to acceptance by the President.

On the other, it has been reported that following Mr. Varma’s resignation on April 9, 2026 “with immediate effect”, his status at the Bar was changed to “active” on resumption of practice. Some of his dues and benefits as a sitting judge have reportedly been stopped since the resignation.
(1) Is Mr. Varma’s resignation subject to acceptance by the President?

Our Constitution vests 13 constitutional functionaries with the “power to resign at will”: the power to demit office at a time of their choosing, without their resignation being subject to acceptance by any authority. They may resign merely by writing under their hand addressed to an authority specified in the Constitution. No further action is necessary. Needing no acceptance, the power to resign at will is an essential safeguard for the independence of these offices. It protects incumbents from being forced to work under coercion, contrary to their conscience.

The offices vesting incumbents with this power are: the President; the Vice-President; the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha; judge of the Supreme Court; judge of High Courts; Governors; the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of a State Assembly; the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of a State Legislative Council; and member of Public Service Commissions.

In contrast, Article 101 (3)(b) of the Constitution expressly says that the resignation of Members of Parliament is subject to acceptance by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, as the case may be. Under Article 190(3)(b), the resignations of members of State Legislative Assemblies and Legislative Councils are likewise subject to acceptance by the Speaker or the Chairman.
A five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Misra (1978) unanimously reaffirmed the power of Supreme Court and High Court judges to resign at will.

Justice S. Murtaza Fazal Ali dissented from the majority Judges who held that a resigning Judge could choose a future date and withdraw the resignation before that date. But Justice Ali reflected the unanimous view of the Bench that no acceptance was needed for resignation of judges. He wrote categorically that “the effectiveness of the resignation does not depend upon the acceptance of the resignation by the President…the resignation acts ex proprio vigore” (automatically without requiring any external action).

At least 12 High Court judges have resigned since 2017. One Supreme Court judge, Justice Dalveer Bhandari, resigned in 2012 to join the International Court of Justice. Publicly available information suggests that these resignations have been handled in compliance with the law described above, coming into effect as the resigning judge stipulated, without the effectiveness of the resignation being dependent on acceptance by the President or by anyone else.
(2) Can Mr. Varma still be held out as a sitting judge; can he continue to draw the benefits of office?

Since Mr. Varma ceased to be a judge on April 9, describing him after that date as a sitting judge of the Allahabad High Court in the Department of Justice’s list or on the website of the Allahabad High Court is clearly wrong.

articles.title: Ethanol tender sparks feedstock concerns as rice gains ground over maize
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Oil Marketing Companies’ (OMCs) latest ethanol procurement tender for Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2026–27 has triggered concerns among grain-based ethanol producers and sections of the sugar industry over feedstock pricing, allocation priorities and the potential implications for the sector.

The tender sets procurement prices at ₹60.32 a litre for surplus foodgrains (SFG), with a stated cap of 108 crore litres for the first three quarters; ₹64 a litre for damaged foodgrains (DFG); and ₹66 a litre for maize, plus an additional ₹2.79 a litre. While ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses has been excluded, C-heavy molasses-based ethanol remains eligible for procurement.

The Grain Ethanol Manufacturers Association (GEMA) has argued that the tender places a disproportionate burden on rice-based feedstocks, particularly SFG and DFG, while potentially weakening maize’s role as an industrial feedstock.
The pricing differential has also created uncertainty over how procurement demand will be distributed among the different feedstock categories.

According to industry estimates, DFG-based ethanol allocation during ESY 2025–26 was approximately 60 crore litres. For ESY 2026–27, the industry anticipates that the allocation could exceed 700 crore litres.

C.K. Jain, president of GEMA, said a balanced ethanol policy must support viable production from both maize and rice, with procurement prices reflecting their different cost structures and allocations providing reasonable visibility to producers. He added that the government and OMCs should review the pricing and allocation framework.

GEMA has also questioned whether maize will receive adequate procurement opportunities under the lowest-price-based allocation mechanism. It has called for greater clarity on the methodology for feedstock-wise allocation and the role envisaged for maize in meeting the country’s ethanol requirements.

The Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) has welcomed the exclusion of ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses, arguing that the approach is consistent with the need to safeguard domestic sugar availability amid uncertainty over the forthcoming crop.
C-heavy molasses-based ethanol, it noted, allows sugar mills to continue contributing to the ethanol-blending programme without diverting recoverable sugar.
However, ISMA has raised concerns over the preferential allocation granted to dedicated ethanol plants holding Long-Term Offtake Agreements under the ESY 2026–27 tender.
While the provision is already in place for the current year, its continuation in subsequent years could hurt the sugar industry, the association said.

articles.title: Data suggests broad-based increase in food prices: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: High-frequency data collected by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for October (till 19th), suggest a broad-based increase in food prices, said RBI officials in the October edition of RBI Bulletin, which was released on Friday (October 23, 2026).

“Among cereals, rice and wheat prices continued to increase. Prices of major pulses also went up sequentially. Edible oil prices also recorded a slow and broad-based increase, led by mustard and palm oil,” they wrote in the ‘State of the Economy’ article.
Among vegetables, while potato prices declined and the pace of onion price increases dropped, tomato prices picked up, they added.

Surprisingly, inflation in rural areas has been getting higher than that in urban areas. Inflation stood at 4.9% and 6.1%, respectively, in urban and rural areas in September. In August, urban and rural inflation stood at 4.3% and 5.2% respectively, the officials stated.
ALSO WATCH The battle against inflation is entering a tougher phase: What it means for you

The majority of States/UTs recorded inflation in the range of 4-6% in September. Inflation ranged from 2.9% to 6.9% across states/UTs. States like Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry recorded inflation in excess of 6% across both rural and urban areas, they pointed out.

Stating that WPI inflation recorded its first double-digit rate in the new series (Base 2022-23) at 11.4% in September 2026, rising from 9.9% in August, reflecting a broad-based increase in prices, they said industrial and farm input costs remained elevated.
Inflation in the Output Producer Price Index surged to 11.4% in September 2026 from 9.8% in August, led by manufacturing products, and mining & quarrying, they said.
As per the article headline, CPI inflation edged up over the months and showed signs of greater generalisation across commodities, calling for a commensurate change in the monetary policy stance.
“The external headwinds are also being dealt with a slew of regulatory measures by the Reserve Bank to curb speculative activity in foreign exchange market,” they stated.

“Strong inflows under FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) and remittance flows strengthened in August. With strong exports growth, the trade deficit narrowed in September,” they added.

The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5% (YoY) in September from 4.8% in August, driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel and core (CPI excluding food and fuel) components.

articles.title: Bharat Petroleum’s net profit dips amid volatile crude prices in Q2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Bharat Petroleum’s standalone net profits in the September-end quarter fell 22.5% on a year-over-year basis as volatile crude prices impacted margins following the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The Mumbai-headquartered refiner’s net profit declined to ₹4,993.17 crore in the reported quarter compared to ₹6,442.5 crore in the same period last year.
The state-owned oil-marketing company’s cost of materials consumed soared 44.2% during the period to ₹74,969 crore.
